solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The noise of a school used to be unending (5)

indicators.note: the word is denied its final letter

blocks.note: SCH is a standard abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: A teacher remembering how loud the playground once was.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides in the first words: a schwa is the neutral vowel sound of unstressed 'a', as in 'about'. 'The noise' wants to be the school's din.
explanation.definitionFit: The schwa is the sound the letter a makes in unstressed syllables, so it is literally the noise of a.

clue.text: Dissolute, was not so old and wise to do this? (3,4,4,4)

definitions.text: Dissolute, was not so old and wise to do this?

indicators.note: dis-solute: the letters are dissolved and remade

explanation.surface: An older, wiser person looking back on the reckless life of their youth.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: someone dissolute who was younger and less wise is exactly who sows wild oats. 'Dissolute' reads as a description, not an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To sow one's wild oats is to live a dissolute life while young and foolish, before settling down.

clue.text: Piscivore caught by another one (5)

indicators.note: the answer is held inside the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words, minus the first three and last one

explanation.surface: One fish-eater being snapped up by another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught by' reads as predator eating prey, but it means held inside: anot(HER ON)e.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a bird that lives on fish, so it is a piscivore.

clue.text: I’ll verify accounts of car stuck on hill (7)

definitions.note: a self-description in the first person: the auditor says 'I'll verify accounts'

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

indicators.note: one piece is attached to the other, car first

explanation.surface: A witness promising to check the reports of a car wedged on a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accounts of car' reads as reports of an accident; the definition is really a first-person job description. A tor is a rocky hilltop in the West of England.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor is the person whose job is to check a firm's accounts.

clue.text: Digital extremist upset by lunatic fringe (9)

indicators.note: the letters go mad and rearrange

blocks.note: to tip is to upset, knock over

explanation.surface: An online zealot rattled by people on the political edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital extremist' sounds like an internet radical, but digital means of the fingers, and the extremity of a finger is its tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A fingertip is the extreme end of a digit.

clue.text: Play heads or tails and lose it (4)

blocks.note: informal: to lose your temper or go mad

explanation.surface: Someone tossing a coin and then losing their temper over the result.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface joins two actions into one story, but each half is a separate sense of FLIP: tossing a coin and snapping in anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Flipping a coin decides heads or tails, and to flip (out) is to lose control.

clue.text: Novel put up as toilet paper source (10)

definitions.note: plural answer; the definition is singular, read as the kind of shop

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up a word writes it bottom to top

blocks.note: the Gents is a men's toilet

explanation.surface: A book so bad it was hung up in the loo as a supply of toilet roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toilet paper' is a false unit: toilet belongs to the wordplay and paper to the definition. A newsagent's is a British shop selling newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsagents are where people buy their newspapers.

clue.text: Key power one has to comprehend source of motivation of second person? (7)

definitions.text: Key power one has to comprehend source of motivation of second person?

indicators.note: the letters so far take the next piece inside them
the first letter of the word

blocks.note: first letter of motivation, taken inside E-P-A
thy is the old second-person possessive

explanation.surface: A question about the key ability needed to understand what drives someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the key power to comprehend another person's motivation is empathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is the ability to understand what another person feels and why they act.

clue.text: Sore loser in 2020? He had to maintain “I won” (9)

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so TRUMP holds I

blocks.note: Donald Trump lost the 2020 US election and disputed it

explanation.surface: Donald Trump in 2020 insisting he had won the election he lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make "I won" look like one phrase, but I is wordplay and only won is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To triumph is to win, so triumphed means won.

clue.text: Perhaps start to make Perry’s media presentation (5,10)

blocks.note: perry is pear cider; you begin by pressing pears, such as the Conference variety

explanation.surface: Perhaps Katy Perry opening her media launch.
explanation.walkthrough: Perry looks like a person's name, but it is pear cider, and Conference is a common British pear variety. 'Perhaps' flags Conference as just one example of a pear.
explanation.definitionFit: A press conference is an event where someone presents to the media.

clue.text: Vile word, spewed with attitude (5,4)

indicators.note: the letters are thrown out in a mess

explanation.surface: Someone spitting out a curse word with real venom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With attitude' reads as 'aggressively', but with is the W the fodder needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A world view is one's general outlook or attitude to life.

clue.text: Prepare two or three? (5)

definitions.note: the second definition gives examples: two and three are each a prime number

blocks.note: to make ready, as a wall before painting or a pump before use
numbers divisible only by themselves and 1; the question mark flags definition by example

explanation.surface: Getting a couple of things ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two or three' reads as 'a few', but it names two particular numbers that share a property.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for prepare, plus a definition by example: 2 and 3 are the first prime numbers.

clue.text: Heading for No 1: “Alien in New York”? No, but it’s in top 100! (6)

definitions.note: a clause describing the answer rather than a noun

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word
the alien goes inside New York

explanation.surface: A chart commentator asking whether an 'Alien in New York' single will reach No 1.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a pop chart, with 'No 1' a chart-topper and 'top 100' the chart; the definition is only that ninety is a number within the first hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is not number one, but it does fall within the top hundred numbers.

clue.text: Crosswords etc in dad’s paper (8)

blocks.note: The Times, the newspaper this very puzzle is in

explanation.surface: The puzzles you find in your father's newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is self-referential: this crossword is in The Times, which is the paper in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: doing crosswords and the like is how people pass their leisure time.

clue.text: Old magic trick failing in the end, dodgily using blue humour? (10)

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter
the letters are arranged in a dodgy way

explanation.surface: A washed-up magician whose trick flops, so he resorts to smutty jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue humour means dirty jokes, but here blue means sad: sad plus funny is tragicomic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tragicomic mixes the sad and the funny, so it uses gloomy humour.

clue.text: Comeback for pasta sauces, price about right for slimmers? (5-4)

indicators.note: a comeback runs the word the other way
about means around, so the price wraps around the letter for right

blocks.note: RAGUS reversed; ragù is an Italian meat sauce
a fee is a price, going around R

explanation.surface: A food trend report: pasta sauces are back, and priced right for dieters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comeback' looks like a revival of pasta sauces, but it tells you to read RAGUS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar-free products are made for people trying to lose weight.

clue.text: Provoke girl to disappear, leaving hospital on ecstasy (9)

indicators.note: the letter for hospital departs from the word
in a down clue, one piece sits on the next

explanation.surface: A young woman slipping out of hospital high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On ecstasy' reads as drugged, but on only places E after the rest in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To galvanise someone is to shock or provoke them into action.

clue.text: Boorish person from tech firm (5)

blocks.note: a lout, named after the brutish human creatures in Gulliver's Travels
the American internet company famous for its web portal

explanation.surface: A rude employee of a technology company.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word serves both halves: Swift's word for a brute, which the internet company took as its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary coinage now used as a plain synonym for a lout, and also the proper name of a web company.

clue.text: Is shirker paid less as retainer? (5)

definitions.note: 'is shirker' stands for 'is a shirker', a verb phrase like idles

indicators.note: the words retain, hold, the answer inside them

blocks.note: the letters span the two words, dropping PA at the start and S at the end

explanation.surface: Asking whether a lazy worker gets a smaller retainer fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retainer' looks like a fee paid to keep someone on, but it indicates that paid less holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who idles is behaving as a shirker.

clue.text: Edit message’s underlying implication (7)

blocks.note: to sub is to subedit, a newspaper editing job
a text is a phone message

explanation.surface: An editor spotting what a message really means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edit' is a verb in the surface, but SUB is newspaper jargon for a sub-editor's work; the ’s just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtext is the meaning that lies beneath what is said.

clue.text: Discover singer Bob’s left out, replaced by double (3,4,2)

indicators.note: the L is taken out and something else put in its place

blocks.note: Bob Geldof, Irish singer and Live Aid organiser
a double is a twin, in L's place

explanation.surface: Finding out a famous singer has been dropped and replaced by a lookalike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' tempts you toward Dylan or Marley, but only GELDOF has an L to swap.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from hunting, where an animal catches a scent on the air, meaning to learn of something.

clue.text: Is America divided by the endless mass, Panama? (7)

definitions.note: the definition is an example: Panama is an isthmus

indicators.note: IS US is split apart with letters inserted
the word drops its last letter

explanation.surface: Asking whether the Americas are cut in two by the great landmass of Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two words are read as one unit that gets split; the question mark flags Panama as an example of the answer, not the thing itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isthmus of Panama is the narrow strip of land joining North and South America.

clue.text: Con ward? (8)

blocks.note: its four letters, which the answer tells you to read backwards
the question mark flags a reverse clue: the reversal instruction is part of the answer itself

explanation.surface: A criminal on a prison ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: the answer, read as an instruction, produces the wordplay. Take DRAW back and you get WARD. A con is a disadvantage, as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the cons in 'pros and cons' are the disadvantages of a choice.

clue.text: Dullness of Proust novel (6)

indicators.note: new, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: A complaint about how tedious a Proust novel is.
explanation.walkthrough: Proust wrote famously long novels, so 'Proust novel' reads as a book; novel is only the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of dull, dazed torpor.

clue.text: Move to the rhythm in Lima? (5)

definitions.note: the second definition is an example: a Lima bean is a pulse

blocks.note: the Lima bean, one kind of edible legume seed; the question mark flags an example

explanation.surface: Dancing in the capital of Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima looks like the Peruvian city, but it is the Lima bean, one kind of pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym for throbbing to a beat, plus a definition by example: the Lima bean is one of the edible legume seeds.

clue.text: What Harris and Lewis combine to make (4)

definitions.text: What Harris and Lewis combine to make

indicators.note: the touching ends of the two names join together

blocks.note: the last two letters of Harris
first letters: the opening two letters of Lewis, where it meets Harris

explanation.surface: A geography question about two places in the Outer Hebrides.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis and Harris are two parts of a single island in Scotland's Outer Hebrides, so the whole clue is also the definition. Where the names meet, harrIS LEwis, they make ISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis and Harris together form one island, an isle.

clue.text: Hit single? Not Careless Whisper (5)

blocks.note: the main side of a vinyl single, the one meant to be the hit
an actor's deliberate murmured remark to the audience, the opposite of a careless whisper

explanation.surface: Quizzing about a hit single that is not George Michael's Careless Whisper.
explanation.walkthrough: Careless Whisper was a George Michael hit, so the clue reads as a music quiz; but an aside is a whisper made on purpose, not carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-side of a single carries the hit, and an actor's aside is a whisper meant for the audience.

clue.text: Fruit of millions held by Zuckerberg, Mark’s fellow billionaire? (9)

indicators.note: M sits inside the billionaire's name

blocks.note: written surname first, as Zuckerberg, Mark is
m = millions, placed between the names

explanation.surface: Mark Zuckerberg's rival tech billionaire enjoying the fruits of his millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zuckerberg, Mark' shows the format, surname then first name, so his fellow billionaire becomes Musk, Elon.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: the muskmelon is one species of sweet melon, which is a fruit.

clue.text: Display glass? (9)

blocks.note: one lens of a pair of glasses; the question mark flags the rare singular

explanation.surface: A shop window made of glass.
explanation.walkthrough: The singular for one lens of a pair of glasses is rare, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a show, and a back-formation from the plural word for eyeglasses.

clue.text: Part of play witnessed by audience (5)

indicators.note: an audience hears, so this is how the word sounds

explanation.surface: A section of a play watched by the people in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By audience' reads as the theatre-goers watching, but it tells you the audience only hears the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: plays are divided into acts, and acts into these shorter units.
